questions.q: Two customer groups have different average order values in your sample. Why isn't that difference alone enough to conclude the email works?
options: Sample averages never match exactly, even when nothing differs, so we must compare the gap to what chance alone produces
Averages are unreliable and should never be compared
Differences only count if the sample has exactly 100 customers
The larger average always wins automatically
questions.explain: Random variation guarantees some gap between any two samples. A hypothesis test asks whether the observed gap is bigger than typical chance gaps.

questions.q: Why do we test the null hypothesis rather than the alternative?
options: The null is a concrete, precise world (no difference) that we can simulate or calculate under
The null is always true
The alternative cannot be written down in words
Testing the alternative is illegal in statistics
questions.explain: 'No difference' pins down one specific world. 'Some difference' could be any size, so it can't be simulated directly.

questions.q: In a permutation test, why is it legitimate to shuffle the 'old' and 'new' labels?
options: It fixes measurement errors in the data
If the email has no effect, the labels carry no information, so any split of the 80 orders is equally plausible
It makes the sample larger
It guarantees a significant result
questions.explain: Under the null the labels are interchangeable. Shuffling shows what gaps luck alone produces.

questions.q: A test fails to reject the null. What is the correct reading?
options: The null hypothesis has been proven true
The alternative has been proven false
The evidence wasn't strong enough to rule out chance; the result is inconclusive
The experiment must be repeated until it rejects
questions.explain: Like 'not guilty' in court, failing to reject is not proof of no effect. The data may simply be too limited.

questions.q: The permutation test rejects the null. Which claim does that result NOT support by itself?
options: The observed gap would be unusual if chance alone were at work
Chance alone is a poor explanation of this gap
The new email caused the difference and the difference is commercially important
The gap is larger than most shuffled gaps
questions.explain: A test speaks to chance only. Cause depends on how the groups were formed, and importance depends on effect size, not on the test.
